findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:90 — `updateDevice` treats `RowsAffected == 0` as "limit reached", but on MySQL (go-sql-driver default) `RowsAffected` returns *changed* rows, not matched rows. When the UPDATE writes identical values (same IP/UA and same-second `DATETIME` truncation of `updated_at`), rowsAffected is 0 and an existing, legitimate device is spuriously denied with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

[Medium/concurrency] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:100-110 — The limit enforcement is a non-atomic count-then-insert: `CountDevices` and the subsequent insert in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` are not wrapped in a transaction or guarded by a lock/conditional insert, so concurrent first-time devices can all observe `count < limit` and insert, overshooting `deviceLimit` under load.

[Medium/performance] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-50 — Device tagging was moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine into the synchronous authentication path. With `deviceLimit > 0`, every local-cache miss now blocks the user request on a `COUNT(*)` over `anon_device` plus a write; denied devices are (likely) never cached, so each subsequent request from them repeats the COUNT + failed UPDATE, adding latency and DB amplification exactly when the limit is saturated.

[Medium/api] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:47-49 — Returning the raw `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` from `Authenticate` aborts the authn chain, but no HTTP error mapping/status is registered for it (it is not `authn.ErrUnauthorized`), so users hitting the limit will get an opaque generic failure (likely a 500) instead of a meaningful 401/403/429 with an explainable message. There is also no operator-facing log/metric at the point of denial.

[Medium/test_gap] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51-68 — Only the "new device rejected at limit" path is tested. There is no test for the allowed path — an existing, recently-updated device being successfully refreshed via `updateDevice` when `count >= deviceLimit` — which is the core new code path (and the one affected by issue 1).

[Low/test_gap] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-50 — No test verifies that `ErrDeviceLimitReached` actually propagates through `TagDevice`/`Anonymous.Authenticate` (e.g. that `tagDeviceUI` wraps/forwards the sentinel error so `errors.Is` matches), nor that the insert path still works when `count < deviceLimit` with a limit configured.

[Low/doc_defect] conf/defaults.ini — The new `device_limit` option under `[auth.anonymous]` is not added to `conf/defaults.ini` (or docs), and the sentinel semantics (0 = unlimited, negative values silently treated as unlimited) are undocumented, making the feature undiscoverable.

[Low/api] packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200 — The TS type is `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined`, but the Go DTO (`frontendsettings.go:195`, no `omitempty`) always serializes the field as a number (0 when unset), so `undefined` can never occur at runtime; consumers also cannot distinguish "not configured" from the 0-sentinel.

[Low/bug] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:16 vs pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go:18 — The 30-day expiration is now duplicated as two independent constants (`anonymousDeviceExpiration` in both packages, replacing the single `thirtyDays`); the enforcement window (count/update), the cleanup retention, and the API listing window can silently drift apart in future changes.

goldens.comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-50 — Device tagging was moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine into the synchronous authentication path. With `deviceLimit > 0`, every local-cache miss now blocks the user request on a `COUNT(*)` over `anon_device` plus a write; denied devices are (likely) never cached, so each subsequent request from them repeats the COUNT + failed UPDATE, adding latency and DB amplification exactly when the limit is saturated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move device tagging from an async goroutine into the synchronous auth path: in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` the `go func(){...context.WithTimeout...TagDevice...}()` block was removed and replaced with a direct `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` call that can now block authentication. The diff also adds a per-tag DB amplification path when `deviceLimit > 0`: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go` now does `CountDevices(...)` and, when saturated, attempts `updateDevice(...)` (an UPDATE + RowsAffected check) and can return `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. That combination is a concrete performance/latency concern created by the change. The claim that denied devices are “likely never cached” is not directly verifiable from the shown diff (cache behavior on error isn’t visible here), but the rest of the finding is grounded.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core regression: when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, Authenticate now returns that error and aborts anonymous authentication, preventing users from authenticating. The candidate additionally focuses on missing HTTP/status mapping and observability, but it still identifies the blocking failure on device-limit hit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51-68 — Only the "new device rejected at limit" path is tested. There is no test for the allowed path — an existing, recently-updated device being successfully refreshed via `updateDevice` when `count >= deviceLimit` — which is the core new code path (and the one affected by issue 1).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new core behavior in `CreateOrUpdateDevice`: when `s.deviceLimit > 0` and `count >= s.deviceLimit`, it calls `s.updateDevice(ctx, device)` (new code in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`). The new test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` (in `database_test.go`) only exercises the rejection case for a *new* device ID at the limit and asserts `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. There is no test covering the intended *allowed* path where an existing device (same `device_id`) is successfully refreshed/updated via `updateDevice` when the limit is reached, i.e., verifying that `rowsAffected > 0` leads to `nil` rather than `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-50 — No test verifies that `ErrDeviceLimitReached` actually propagates through `TagDevice`/`Anonymous.Authenticate` (e.g. that `tagDeviceUI` wraps/forwards the sentinel error so `errors.Is` matches), nor that the insert path still works when `count < deviceLimit` with a limit configured.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior where `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` can be returned from `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (via `updateDevice`) and is now propagated up through `AnonDeviceService.TagDevice` (it now `return err` after `tagDeviceUI` failure) and then handled specially in `Anonymous.Authenticate` (returns the error when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`). Existing tests only cover the store-level limit (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` asserts `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`) and do not exercise the propagation path through `TagDevice`/`Authenticate`, nor the success insert path when a nonzero limit is configured but `count < deviceLimit` (all `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` tests use `setting.NewCfg()` with default limit 0). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] conf/defaults.ini — The new `device_limit` option under `[auth.anonymous]` is not added to `conf/defaults.ini` (or docs), and the sentinel semantics (0 = unlimited, negative values silently treated as unlimited) are undocumented, making the feature undiscoverable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new INI key read (`anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)`) and threads it through as `AnonymousDeviceLimit`, but no change to `conf/defaults.ini` or documentation appears in the provided PR diff, making the option harder to discover. Also, the runtime semantics are `deviceLimit > 0` enforced (otherwise unlimited), so `0` and negative values both effectively mean “unlimited,” which is non-obvious and not documented in-code here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200 — The TS type is `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined`, but the Go DTO (`frontendsettings.go:195`, no `omitempty`) always serializes the field as a number (0 when unset), so `undefined` can never occur at runtime; consumers also cannot distinguish "not configured" from the 0-sentinel.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows the backend always provides `AnonymousDeviceLimit` as a concrete `int64` in `FrontendSettingsDTO` (no `omitempty`) and `Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is always set via `MustInt64(0)` (so “unset” becomes `0`). That means the frontend cannot distinguish “not configured” from an explicit `0` limit, and the TS type `number | undefined` does not match the backend contract for this PR (it will be a number in the JSON). However, this is more of an API/type-semantics mismatch than a directly verifiable runtime breakage in this diff (frontend also initializes `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:16 vs pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go:18 — The 30-day expiration is now duplicated as two independent constants (`anonymousDeviceExpiration` in both packages, replacing the single `thirtyDays`); the enforcement window (count/update), the cleanup retention, and the API listing window can silently drift apart in future changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce two separate constants with the same meaning: `anonymousDeviceExpiration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go` (used for CountDevices/update window) and another `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go` (used for the ListDevices window). This isn’t a current functional bug because both are currently identical, but it is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue created by the change: future edits could update one window without updating the other, causing API listing and enforcement/retention behavior to diverge silently.
